chunk_map.heading: Sharpen the plan with two reads (title/lede)
Scan the plan before you push back
Phase 4: Walk down the unresolved branches
Answer the branches that change what "done" means
Switch to a picker if you prefer one
Stop when the plan is good enough to generate
Run the original grill-me if you want the full hour
Phase 5: Stop, then surface the patterns

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call: chunk 3 "Scan the plan before you push back", line 36: "Scan it against the five things a good plan has, and start where a sharper answer would most change execution." -- "the five things" is never enumerated or named anywhere in this file, a genuine per-file gap under a strict sequential-deck read. Holds inside because maintainer line 115 (dated 2026-08-25) documents this as the deliberate cut-down replacing a full walkthrough: "file-not-chat plus the pointer at the lecture's five things... do not re-add a notice-which walkthrough of the five things -- that re-teaches the lecture's checklist ONE SLIDE AFTER it was taught" -- i.e. the maintainer's own model has `when-a-plan-is-good.md`'s five-things slide as the immediately preceding beat in the same module's deck order, which §1's module-arc-beats carve-out ("module include-order = deck order more generally") is built to cover, even though its stated examples don't name this exact lecture-then-exercise shape (flagged as a todo below). All other chunks check clean: chunk 2 line 27 "Drop your task after the colon" resolves against the prompt fence in the SAME chunk (line 29), the passing same-chunk shape per §12; "the second read"/"the walk-down" (chunks 5-9) resolve against chunk 0's lede ("a walk-down three questions at a time"); "Phase 5" named forward at chunk 8 line 78 is a heading name, not a positional pointer; "the way you did" (chunk 5 line 54) is the student's own prior action inside this same exercise, not an external referent.

No positional cross-file callback ("the opening lecture said...", "as shown earlier") anywhere in the body -- grepped for above/below/earlier-in-module phrasing, zero hits. Sole cross-file reference: chunk 9, line 83: "Credit: Matt Pocock for the original [`grill-me`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/62f43a1/skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md) skill." -- names source and author directly with a pinned commit link, the rule's own passing shape. Chunk 3's "five things" line (rule 1) carries no positional language at all (no "as taught earlier") -- it is a bare content assumption, §1's territory, not a §2 positional pointer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 12 body `##` headings checked: 5 are "Phase N:" labels (chunks 1, 2, 4, 5, 11), the remaining 7 are imperatives ("Scan the plan before you push back," "Answer the branches that change what 'done' means," "Switch to a picker if you prefer one," "Stop when the plan is good enough to generate," "Run the original grill-me if you want the full hour," "Approve," "Compare what each read caught"). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Audited all 20 body bullets against the three classes (doctrine restatement, self-referential design commentary, aphorism kicker). Two closest calls, both hold inside: chunk 11 line 97 "Don't execute the plan. The work of making it good is the exercise." reads (b)-adjacent but stays inside because it directly justifies the immediately preceding instruction (why not execute) rather than commenting on the training's own pedagogical design -- maintainer line 128 confirms it is the trainer's own anticipated-FAQ answer, not filler, and it is this file's only articulation of the reason. Chunk 12 line 106 "Neither read needs to be complete. Paired, they surface the sharpenings worth making before generation." could look like a restatement of chunk 0's What-you-build line, but maintainer line 121 (2026-08-02) documents this exact placement as deliberate: What-you-build states only the activity, and the pairing's VALUE claim is placed here at the P5 compare beat on purpose, its first appearance in the file. No other bullet matches any of the three classes.

todos.note: "Scan it against the five things a good plan has" resolves only via a cross-file adjacency argument (the lecture `when-a-plan-is-good.md` is assumed to sit immediately before this exercise in the same module's deck order per maintainer line 115) -- a real, dated, reasoned maintainer call, but the compendium's stated §1 carve-outs (session artifacts, arc-earned spine vocabulary, module-arc beats in openers/closers) don't literally name "content taught in an immediately-preceding lecture within the same module." Non-blocking: the resolution is sound under the carve-outs' own stated general principle ("module include-order = deck order more generally") and the maintainer has explicitly reasoned about deck adjacency. Fix: name this shape explicitly in §1's carve-out list so a future judge doesn't have to re-derive the analogy.

The check_pedagogy §34 task-sizing exception's named-location list ("## Prework, ## Bring to Module N, or ## Next") doesn't literally cover an exercise's own "## Phase 1: Bring a real task" heading, even though the bolded floor+ceiling sentence here ("A one-line fix is too small for plan mode; a refactor whose outcome you can't hold in your head is too big.") matches the exception's function exactly (task selection drives this beat's outcome). Non-blocking: §9 itself says to recognise the shape by function, not wording, so this resolves cleanly -- but a future judge pattern-matching the location list alone could misfire here. Fix: add an exercise-Phase-1 example to §9's exception text alongside the Prework/Bring-to-Module-N/Next list.
